name: Audio-only (Live)
explanation: This criterion applies to live audio content that has no video component at all — for example, a live radio broadcast streamed on a website, or a live call-in show. It requires an alternative that presents equivalent information to that live audio as it happens. Because the content is live, there's no chance to author a transcript in advance, so in practice this means real-time captioning or live transcription of the audio stream. This is the live counterpart to SC 1.2.1 (Audio-only, Prerecorded), which allows a transcript written after the fact because the audio isn't changing — here there is no 'after the fact' until the broadcast ends. It's also distinct from SC 1.2.4 (Captions, Live), which covers live content with a video track. This criterion is specifically for live audio with no video at all.
whoItAffects: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users listening to a live radio stream or a call-in show have no way to follow along in real time unless a live transcript is provided. Waiting for a transcript afterward isn't equivalent when the value of the content, like a live Q&A, is in following it as it happens. People in sound-off environments, such as an open office, can read the live text feed instead. Non-native speakers and some users with cognitive or learning disabilities also benefit from being able to read fast or accented live speech as text rather than relying on audio alone.

codeExample.bad: Live: Morning Markets Radio
codeExample.good: Live: Morning Markets Radio

howToTest: Find a live audio-only stream on the site and check whether a live transcript or real-time captioning feed is offered alongside it. Open that text feed and listen to the audio while watching the text, confirming that new text appears within a short delay rather than staying blank. It fails if the only alternative offered is a transcript that becomes available after the stream is over, or if no text alternative exists at all — the whole point is being able to follow the live content as it happens.

check.question: A website streams a live, audio-only call-in radio show with no video component. According to SC 1.2.9, what is required?
choices: A transcript published on the website after the show ends
A real-time text alternative (such as live captioning or live transcription) presented while the broadcast is happening
Nothing, since SC 1.2.1 already covers audio-only content
Captions burned into a video player showing the hosts
